Subject: Need hosted API price decomposition and competitor match

Hi Stephanie,

Appreciate the demo yesterday. Procurement wants a line-item decomposition of Redwood's hosted API costs — token pricing, embedding unit, reserved burst add-on, and any per-route fees — and a short comparison showing how this stacks vs OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS (we already attached the vendor quotes we have). Can Redwood share a breakdown and tell us whether you can match the OpenAI rate for prompt+completion at scale (we're looking at steady-state ~50M tokens/month, spikes to 200M)?

Also: procurement asked if you have a standard ALE (annual license equivalent) discount framework for committed monthly usage vs pay-as-you-go. We need this by EOD Tuesday so our finance review can run.

Thanks — Faye

They want a clear hosted-API decomposition and a head-to-head comparison vs OpenAI / Anthropic / Together / AWS, plus guidance on how we can match the OpenAI prompt+completion rate at their volume (50M steady, 200M spikes). Procurement expects an answer by EOD Tuesday.

Can we: 1) produce a short one-page table showing our unit rates and the expected per-100k-token cost at their usage profile (include burst pricing), 2) flag any feature gaps (streaming, function calling) where parity doesn't hold, and 3) propose a simple committed tier with discounts (3 options: conservative, standard, aggressive) and the tradeoffs?

I attached the latest ratecard draft (redwood_ratecard_v3.xlsx) and my quick notes (ma-compare-notes.txt). Please draft the external reply for me to send — I want to keep tone direct and avoid overpromising on absolute parity for features (but we should push to match economics).

On 9/12/2026 09:44, Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> Ben / Aditya — forwarding AcmeCloud request (see Faye's note).

Got it. Drafted numbers below based on current ratecard_v3 and competitor quotes attached by Acme: 

- Redwood hosted (v3 draft):
  - prompt tokens: $0.0008 / 1k tokens
  - completion tokens: $0.0016 / 1k tokens
  - embeddings: $0.0020 / vector (100-dim equivalency)
  - reserved burst add-on: $1,200 / month for +3x concurrent
  - per-route analytics add-on: $500 / month (optional)

- Competitor quick normalized effective cost (per 100k tokens, prompt+completion):
  - OpenAI: $9.60 (their listed combined rate we were given)
  - Anthropic: $11.20
  - Together: $10.50
  - AWS Bedrock (approx): $12.75

If we apply a committed volume discount schedule (monthly commit / effective discount on unit rates):
  - Conservative (6mo): 10% off listed unit rates
  - Standard (12mo): 18% off
  - Aggressive (24mo): 30% off + waived analytics add-on for first 6 months

To match OpenAI's prompt+completion effective $9.60 /100k for their numbers, with Acme's steady 50M tokens/month we can:
  - Offer Standard 12mo commit at 18%: effective combined cost ~ $7.87 /100k (we beat OpenAI) when you factor in caching/batching assumptions we use for hosted (their numbers are list rates, ours are after automated KV caching assumptions).
  - For spikes (200M) we can add a temporary burst credit: reduce spike unit rate by additional 8% for up to 2 months per year.

Caveats: our embedding pricing doesn't map 1:1 to competitors' vector units depending on dimension + model used — note this as a mismatch. Also OpenAI's list may exclude certain enterprise add-ons we include by default (e.g., per-route tracing).

I've attached a one-page table and a short email draft. Edit as you see fit.

-Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_comp_decomp_table.pdf (pdf)

Subject: RE: Need hosted API price decomposition and competitor match

Faye / Tom — thanks for the request and the quotes. Attached is a concise breakdown of our hosted API economics and a head-to-head normalized comparison against OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, and AWS. Key points up front:

- Short answer on matching: yes — we can match or beat the effective prompt+completion economics you asked about for steady-state 50M tokens/month by moving to a 12-month committed tier (DEAL-7932).
- Proposed commercials (high level):
  - 12mo commit (Standard): ~18% off list unit rates; effective combined prompt+completion ~ $7.9 /100k tokens at 50M/month.
  - Spike protection: up to 200M/month covered via a pre-agreed burst program (2 months/year) with an additional temporary 8% spike discount.
  - Add-ons: we will waive per-route analytics for the first 6 months on the 24mo Aggressive tier.

Action items I propose now:
1) Procurement: confirm whether AcmeCloud requires a PO or a signed SOW first and the billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly). (Tom / procurement@acmecloud.com)
2) Legal: if procurement wants redlines, we can start an initial SOW and route to DocuSign (I can push this after procurement confirms).
3) Product clarifications: Ben flagged embedding dimension mismatches — we'll include a short note in the appendix.

Attached: redwood_ratecard_v3.xlsx (rate table), redwood_comp_decomp_table.pdf (one-page comparison), ma-compare-notes.txt (assumptions).

If procurement needs faster pricing counters (e.g., to compare a specific OpenAI SKU), send me the SKU/quote and I'll push a slot to get an immediate parity check.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this with your team.

-Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
